Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (SPICE, OMol25) and numerous baselines (MACE, eSEN, UMA, EquiformerV2, etc.) in both Conservative and Direct settings

No ablation studies isolating contributions of EAAS vs. fused kernel; Figure 3 tensor product benchmarks limited to 1000 operations; training throughput not evaluated

strengths: Addresses a genuine practical bottleneck in equivariant GNNs through hardware-aware kernel design, achieving substantial 20× TFLOPS improvement and enabling inference on 100k-atom systems
Mathematically rigorous with complete formal derivations (Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3) and careful handling of parity selection rules in SO(2) basis reduction
Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning multiple scales, datasets (SPICE, OMol25), and inference scenarios with detailed appendices on experimental setup
Demonstrates genuine practical value with real speedups validated across different system sizes and neighbor counts
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: EAAS is an incremental refinement of eSCN's SO(2) reduction; on-the-fly attention is a straightforward application of FlashAttention; node-centric factorization is from E2Former (Li et al. 2025). Primarily an engineering contribution rather than methodological advance

Claims of 'superior performance' are unsupported or contradicted by results: Table 1 shows eSEN-Cons (0.23/6.36) outperforms E2V2-Cons (0.57/7.80) on SPICE; Table 2 shows eSEN-sm-cons (1.27/8.25) beats E2V2-Cons (2.09/8.38) on OMol25 energies. Paper conflates speedup gains with accuracy improvements

Critical technical detail inadequately explained: the geometric bias b(r_ij) in Eq. (7) appears to be a learned function that could break strict equivariance. Paper claims it 'carries no angular momentum' without specifying its parameterization or validating equivariance preservation

Missing essential ablation studies: no individual component analysis (EAAS vs. on-the-fly attention), no expressivity analysis of SO(2) vs. SO(3), no systematic study of accuracy-speed tradeoffs. Cannot determine which components drive results

Incomplete reproducibility: code URL missing from page 1 ('available at' with no link); Triton kernel source not provided; hyperparameters for b(r_ij) and φ(r_ij) unspecified; training details (optimizer, schedules, seeds) not documented

Benchmark limitations undermine claims: Table 3 uses only synthetic FCC carbon lattices unrepresentative of diverse molecules; only inference speeds reported, not training; eSEN-Cons missing from Table 3 despite strong SPICE/OMol25 performance
Overstated O(|V|) memory complexity claim: bound is SRAM-dependent and hardware-specific. No analysis of behavior when neighbor aggregation exceeds available SRAM or guidance on practical constraints
No numerical stability analysis for streaming softmax formulation (Eqs. 15-17) or gradient flow through on-the-fly computation, despite this being critical for practical training
Insufficient clarity on E2Former-V2 vs. E2Former-V1 differences: if V1 already provided node-centric factorization, what is the fundamental algorithmic innovation in V2?

strengths: Significant practical impact: achieves ~20× speedup in TFLOPS and scales to 100k atoms where competitors fail with OOM, addressing a genuine scalability bottleneck in equivariant architectures

Rigorous mathematical foundation with detailed derivations of pole sparsity lemma, parity selection rules, and proof that SO(3) tensor products can be implemented via rotation conjugation and sparse re-indexing (Proposition 4.3)
Comprehensive experimental validation across SPICE and OMol25 datasets with ~10 competing baselines, including physical validation via MD simulations showing improved structural accuracy
Well-specified algorithmic contributions with clear pseudocode (Algorithm 1) and extensive implementation details in appendices, enabling reproducibility

Effective hardware-software co-design: custom Triton kernel successfully applies FlashAttention streaming principles to sparse equivariant attention, achieving substantial improvements in compute utilization visible in throughput curves

Strong empirical results demonstrating both accuracy and efficiency: 48% Energy MAE improvement on SPICE Dimers vs MACE-Large; competitive 1.27 meV/atom on OMol25; 3× faster inference than next-best method at 100k atoms
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: EAAS builds on eSCN's SO(2) sparsification and standard Wigner-6j identities, on-the-fly kernel is direct application of FlashAttention principles, and node-centric factorization comes from E2Former (2025); contribution is primarily engineering/integration rather than algorithmic innovation

Missing critical ablation studies: cannot isolate contributions of EAAS vs. kernel improvements; no quantification of computational overhead for alignment rotation computation or CG coefficient precomputation costs

Backward pass efficiency completely unaddressed: only forward pass (Algorithm 1) specified; gradient computation cost and training throughput not discussed despite 'accelerating inference' claims requiring training validation

Incomplete expressivity analysis: unclear whether SO(2) reduction vs full SO(3) limits model capacity; improved SPICE results may reflect better implementation rather than superior expressivity; E2V2-Direct outperforming E2V2-Cons in Table 2 suggests unexplained architectural differences

Experimental setup concerns: Figure 1 benchmark uses fixed K=64, H=16 without sensitivity analysis; Table 3 large-scale benchmarks use synthetic FCC carbon systems unrepresentative of real molecular diversity; results are H20 GPU-specific with no portability discussion

Incomplete reproducibility details: Triton kernel code not provided; alignment rotation computation strategy unspecified (SVD vs optimized routine?); CG coefficient handling (precomputation, caching, memory layout) not described; training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, scheduler) for SPICE/OMol25 missing

strengths: Rigorous mathematical foundation with complete proofs: Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.3 are correctly derived and well-presented, with thorough appendix derivations showing how pole sparsity of spherical harmonics enables sparse re-indexing.

Well-engineered systems contribution: The streaming on-the-fly equivariant attention kernel (Algorithm 1) thoughtfully adapts FlashAttention principles to equivariant networks with online softmax for numerical stability and SRAM-aware execution.
Significant practical impact: Achieves 20× speedup in sparse attention and linear O(|V|) memory scaling, enabling inference on previously infeasible 100k-atom systems on commodity GPUs.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets (SPICE, OMol25, OC20), extensive ablation studies (Table 4) isolating component contributions, scaling analysis with memory tracking, and molecular dynamics validation against experimental data.

Strong reproducibility: Detailed algorithmic descriptions, promised code release, complete hyperparameter specifications (Tables 9-10), extensive appendices addressing sensitivity analysis and implementation details.

Competitive accuracy maintenance: On SPICE, E2V2-Conservative achieves best-in-class energy MAE across most subsets; on OMol25 matches eSEN-small (1.27 vs 1.16 meV/atom) while dramatically improving scalability.
weaknesses: Moderate novelty with incremental advancement: The core node-centric factorization (Eq. 5) originates from E2Former (Li et al. 2025); this work primarily optimizes its implementation. Pole sparsity properties of spherical harmonics are classical mathematics. The contribution is systems-level engineering rather than algorithmic innovation.

Overstated sparsity narrative: EAAS still uses Clebsch-Gordan coefficients (Eq. 13) with deterministic sparsity patterns rather than eliminating dense computation; it avoids summing zeros but doesn't fundamentally transform the operation. Alone, EAAS provides only 1.5-3.6× speedup (Table 3); the dominant 20× gain comes from Triton kernel fusion.

Incompletely analyzed expressivity trade-offs: Replaces explicit value-path non-linearity (S² gating in EquiformerV2/eSEN) with attention-based non-linearity (Eq. 34-35) for efficiency. While labeled 'comparable accuracy' in Appendix D, results are mixed (Table 1 shows eSEN-Cons sometimes better on force MAE). The expressivity cost should be more prominent in main text.

Limited scope and applicability: Benefits materialize only for k ≥ 50-100 neighbors (Appendix E); performs comparably or worse for sparse graphs (k < 10). Specialized to 3D molecular systems with cutoff-based neighbors; unclear generalization to other graph domains. GPU optimizations tuned to H20; hardware generalization unexamined.

Experimental limitations and unfair comparisons: (1) Different baselines trained with different hyperparameters preventing fair comparison; (2) Some methods encounter OOM preventing head-to-head evaluation at large scales; (3) Table 5 conflates model differences with implementation choices by comparing Direct vs Conservative modes; (4) Appendix J shows sparse kernel ~100× slower than dense FlashAttention per-kernel throughput, limiting practical ceiling.

Insufficient molecular dynamics validation: Water RDF tested on single system; protein dynamics only 2ns with AlphaFold initialization, not truly validating force accuracy for diverse biomolecular systems. No comparison of MD trajectories to experimental reference data.

Incomplete limitation discussion: No systematic guidance on when to use E2Former-V2 vs alternatives. Memory-throughput-accuracy trade-offs not quantified. Failure modes and dataset characteristics enabling underperformance not discussed. Training-time efficiency absent.

Presentation issues: EAAS intuition (why axis-alignment helps) relegated to appendix; early sections mathematically dense; the '20×' speedup in Figure 1 refers only to sparse attention kernel, overstating full forward-pass gains. Notation inconsistency between ⊗ and @.

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Correctly identifies O(|E|) edge-centric bottleneck as a genuine practical limitation in equivariant GNNs that inhibits scaling to large systems
Sound mathematical foundations: Lemma 4.1 (pole sparsity) and Proposition 4.3 are rigorously derived; connection to CG coefficient selection rules is clear and correct

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Thorough benchmarks against diverse baselines (MACE, eSEN, UMA, EquiformerV2), detailed throughput scaling analysis, component ablation isolating EAAS vs. kernel contributions, and MD validation
Practical impact and scalability: Demonstrates scaling to 100k atoms—impressive for transformer-style architectures and enables previously infeasible applications like large protein MD simulations
Hardware-aware systems perspective: Focuses on SRAM utilization, kernel fusion, and memory I/O optimization—important practical considerations often overlooked in pure ML papers
Reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters (Tables 9-10), comprehensive appendices, code release promised, and generally clear presentation with informative figures
weaknesses: Overstated accuracy preservation claims: Title and abstract claim 'preserves predictive accuracy' but Appendix D reveals deliberate trade-off where value-path non-linearity is reorganized away from S² gating into attention construction. On OC20 S2EF-2M (Table 8), E2V2 shows measurable accuracy penalties (287 meV vs 285 for EquiformerV2, 21.80 meV/Å vs 20.46). This design compromise should be disclosed prominently in main text, not buried in appendix

Misleading attribution of speedups to EAAS: Table 4 ablation shows EAAS alone cannot prevent OOM at 10k atoms—the Triton kernel is the true bottleneck. EAAS provides only ~1.5× speedup while kernel achieves 20×. Title emphasizes EAAS but it is secondary; the real contribution is engineering the fused kernel to avoid O(|E|) edge tensor materialization. This reframing is necessary for honest attribution

Critical neighbor-density limitation understated: Appendix E reveals the method only outperforms edge-centric baselines when k ≥ 10-20 neighbors. Table 6-7 show E2V2 at k=2 is actually slower (11.7 vs 14.2 samples/s). While k=30-100 is typical for real systems, this dependency is a fundamental limitation that should be in the main narrative, not appendix only

Incomplete non-linearity trade-off analysis: Equations (34-35) show σ and radial features ϕ(r_ij) replace S² equivariant gating on edge features, but no ablation quantifying expressivity loss. No investigation of: (1) how scalar attention restriction affects anisotropic interaction learning, (2) gradient flow through online softmax (Algorithm 1), (3) numerical stability implications for double-precision molecular modeling, (4) why expressivity impact is minimal on OMol25 if this is a real trade-off

Memory complexity claims lack rigor: Claims O(|V|) activation memory but analysis covers forward pass only. Training memory requirements with backpropagation through fused kernels unexplored—gradient storage during backward pass could be substantial. Figure 3d appears to be forward-only measurements. No analysis of training vs. inference memory trade-offs

Weak MD simulations validation: Figure 4a shows water RDF curves visually close between E2V2 and MACE-OFF with no quantitative discrepancy metrics. Figure 4b shows only 2 ns simulation—rigorous validation requires: ensemble statistics, energy conservation analysis, longer trajectories (≥10 ns), thermodynamic properties comparison. Current validation is superficial for claims of 'physical fidelity'

Missing critical ablations: No quantification of non-linearity reorganization impact (Appendix D design choice), no sensitivity analysis for 128 attention heads (Table 10), no exploration of degree combinations beyond (256x0e + 256x1e + 256x2e), no investigation of the critical 'tp_type=QKdotS alpha+triton' configuration variants

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Table 1 has many missing eSEN-Cons entries. Why incomplete head-to-head comparison with a key related work? Table 5 speedups are system-size dependent (3× at 100k vs 3-4× at 1k atoms) but presented as uniform. Appendix J (Table 12) shows kernel is much slower than dense FlashAttention (1.951 vs 38.600 TFLOPS at large scale)—this fundamental trade-off between asymptotic scaling and constant factors deserves prominent discussion

Limited algorithmic novelty: EAAS applies known techniques (pole sparsity from solid harmonics, basis alignment). Streaming attention uses standard online softmax. Primary contribution is systems-level engineering of Triton kernels, not fundamental algorithmic advancement. For ICML main research track, this is incremental given E2Former already proved node-centric feasibility

Overstated generalization: Benchmarks (Figure 1, Table 5) primarily use synthetic FCC carbon with ~50 neighbors. Real systems have diverse geometries, bonding patterns, and neighbor distributions. Generalization to varied realistic chemical systems unclear. OC20 S2EF-2M results (Table 8) show E2V2 below strong baselines, contradicting universal accuracy preservation claims

Backward pass complexity not addressed: Algorithm 1 describes forward pass only. Gradient computation through fused kernel efficiency unexplored. Training convergence speed not benchmarked—only inference throughput shown. This is critical for practical adoption where training cost often dominates
Code availability issue: States 'released code can be found at [URL]' but URL is blank, preventing reproducibility verification and independent validation of results

strengths: Addresses a critical practical bottleneck in equivariant GNNs by eliminating O(|E|) edge materialization, enabling 100k atom systems vs ~50k for prior methods
Strong mathematical foundation with rigorous derivations (Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3) and comprehensive proofs in appendices

Impressive experimental validation: 20× inference speedup, 16.9× memory reduction, scales to 100k atoms where prior methods OOM, with component ablation clearly showing necessity of both EAAS and Triton fusion
Physically validated via MD simulations (water RDF reproduction, 30k atom protein stability), confirming practical correctness
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, timing protocols, and implementation details; honest discussion of efficiency/expressivity trade-offs and neighbor-density sensitivity
Novel integration of EAAS algebraic sparsification with fused Triton kernels, adapting FlashAttention-style streaming to equivariant models
weaknesses: Claimed 'theoretical exactness' is overstated: non-linearity reorganization (Eqs. 34–35) represents an efficiency/expressivity trade-off vs EquiformerV2/eSEN's edge-level gating, not exact equivalence
Modest accuracy improvements: SPICE results inconsistent across subsets (some worsen), OMol25 competitive with eSEN-small but not clearly superior, OC20 comparable to baselines
Limited theoretical novelty: core factorization (Eq. 5) from E2Former; EAAS builds on existing SO(2) reductions (eSCN, EquiformerV2); main contribution is implementation optimization

Incomplete experimental coverage: no training time analysis, MD validation limited to 2 ns trajectories on single protein, synthetic FCC carbon benchmarks may not represent chemical diversity, missing failure-mode analysis
Irregular gather operations in Triton kernel substantially slower than dense FlashAttention (Table 12: ~2 TFLOPS vs ~38 TFLOPS), limiting absolute performance

Practical limitations underexplored: edge-centric methods faster for sparse graphs (k<10), custom GROMACS integration limits reproducibility, code not available at review time, GPU-specific (H20) results generalizability unclear
